notes.title: v1.1.0 - Spout video routing
notes.content:
This update adds support for sending and receiving real-time video between Vinyl Reality and other applications (ex: OBS, Resolume, TouchDesigner, Processing) using [url=https://spout.zeal.co/]Spout[/url]. 

Spout uses the GPU to send real-time video between Windows applications with [b]near-zero latency or overhead[/b].

Video can be [b]sent to Spout from the spectator cameras[/b] in all environments in Vinyl Reality, including custom ones created with the SDK.

Vinyl Reality can also [b]receive video from Spout[/b] and display it on the [b]screens in the Streaming Studio and Indoor Rave[/b] environments.

[b]Possible use cases for Spout in Vinyl Reality:[/b]
[list]
[*] Displaying custom visuals in the environments by receiving video from a VJ application
[*] Customizing your video streams by sending video to another application and adding effects
[*] Sending video directly to OBS for streaming
[/list]
For more details on how to configure Spout in Vinyl Reality, be sure to check out the[url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=spout] relevant documentation[/url].

[previewyoutube=OFA0yF4KANc;full][/previewyoutube]
The second video is a bit more technical and gives a quick [b]overview of all the DJ equipment currently available[/b] in the application:

[h2]Mod.io[/h2]

To make it easier to [b]share, discover and download user generated content[/b] for Vinyl Reality, I’ve setup a page for the application on [url=https://vinylreality.mod.io/]mod.io[/url], a cross platform mod API.

Content creators will be encouraged to upload their content to this page going forward, so that all of the [b]custom environments and slipmats[/b] for Vinyl Reality are [b]easily accessible in one place[/b]. An account is [u][b]not[/b][/u] needed to download content, but is required to upload it.

All of the custom content for Vinyl Reality can now be found at: [b][url=https://vinylreality.mod.io/]https://vinylreality.mod.io/[/url][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/b62bc930eecce0ef877c8a722b7c59cf228e4851.jpg[/img]

[h3]Installing custom content[/h3]

For the time being, installing user generated content, still requires the files to be [b]downloaded manually[/b] from the mod.io page, and then [b]extracted and copied into the correct directory[/b].

[b]Install instructions for custom content[/b] can be found on the [b][url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=custom_content]documentation wiki[/url][/b].

I hope to be able to integrate the mod.io API into Vinyl Reality at some point though, so that in the future content can be browsed and managed directly from inside the application.

[h2]Attic Environment[/h2]

Some users might fondly remember the Attic environment which was included in [b]early versions[/b] of Vinyl Reality, but was replaced by the Black Box and Streaming Studio in a recent update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/4efbbbf9cb8263570b6f1e5dff872e373a51aee5.jpg[/img]

After making a few tweaks, this environment is now available again as a [b]separate add-on[/b] and can also be downloaded from the mod.io page: https://vinylreality.mod.io/attic

notes.title: Audio filter effect and performance improvements
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/b3f67ba864e98a2f64d78b0f2c314221def582af.jpg[/img]

[h3]Low and High-Pass Filter[/h3]

This release adds a new knob to each [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=mixer_input_control_overview]mixer channel[/url], which combines a [b]low and high-pass filter[/b].

Turning the knob [b]clockwise[/b] from the 12 o’clock position activates the [b]high-pass filter[/b] (HPF), increasing the cutoff frequency from 20 to 22000hz when completely turned.

Turning the knob [b]counter-clockwise[/b], actives the [b]low-pass filter[/b] (LPF), decreasing the cutoff frequency from 22000hz down to 20hz.

While the filter is active, the LED ring on the bottom of the knob is illuminated in blue.

The filter’s [b]resonance[/b] and [b]attenuation slope[/b] can also be configured in the [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=mixer_settings]mixer’s settings panel.[/url]

[h3]Known issues[/h3]

[b]Cross-platform Oculus avatars[/b] are currently [b]not loading correctly[/b]. This issue is also affecting other applications and games, and is most likely caused by a problem with downloading the required assets from Oculus servers. 
I’ve contacted Oculus about the issue and hope it will be resolved on their end soon.

[h3]Full Release Notes[/h3][list]
[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Added low and high-pass filter knob to each channel
[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Improved 3 band EQ knob sensitivity
[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Added filter resonance and slope to user settings
[*] [b]Tech:[/b] Optimized performance
[/list]

notes.title: Environments overhaul and streaming improvements
notes.content:
After two beta tests, the final version of [b]update 1.3.0[/b] is finally here! Here’s a quick overview of what’s new.

[h2]New Environments[/h2][h3]Streaming Studio[/h3][list][*] A customizable environment with audio reactive video playback and lights
[*] Best suited for video recordings or live streams
[*] Optimized to run smoothly on machines meeting the minimum specs
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/7ae3335ba7bf59e973d1636eb5ad6a73ae744f6d.jpg[/img]

The [b]Streaming Studio[/b] environment is specifically designed for streaming, by making it more visually interesting for people watching a video stream or recording made with Vinyl Reality, from outside of VR on a 2D screen. 

Users can customize the streaming studio environment by[url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=how_to_play_custom_videos_on_the_audio_reactive_screens] playing their own videos on the screens surrounding the DJ booth[/url]. More customization features might be added in upcoming updates.

[h3]Black Box[/h3][list][*] A minimal, low-lit environment
[*] Best suited for long recording or practice sessions
[*] Optimized for performance
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/c41933004552c14948f14045ac59572ef31071e3.jpg[/img]

The [b]Black Box[/b] environment was designed primarily with performance in mind, and should provide a very smooth DJing experience even on systems that only meet the minimum requirements. 

These two new environments replace the existing Attic and Recording Studio environments, but the plan is to make these available again as separate downloads in the near future, so they can be loaded as a custom environment.

[h2]Streaming Cameras[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/0beeb08ec093658970777f148c3d0e03b67a1d30.jpg[/img]

To give users more control over how streams are recorded, each environment now contains two spectator cameras that can be freely positioned anywhere inside the DJ booth. 
Both cameras can be activated using the existing [b]streaming console.[/b] The camera to the left of the DJ gear is assigned to button number 3 on the streaming console and the one to right to button number 4.

For more information on how to use all of these new features, be sure to check out the online documentation for this update: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=early_access_v1.3.0f1

notes.title: More streaming improvements and a new environment – Beta round 2
notes.content:
I wanted to give users more control over how streams are recorded, so I decided to add a new type of spectator camera that can be positioned anywhere in the environment and is activated using the existing streaming console. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/0beeb08ec093658970777f148c3d0e03b67a1d30.jpg[/img]

Each environment now contains two of these new user controllable cameras, one to the left of the DJ gear and one to the right. The left one is assigned to [b]button number 3[/b] on the streaming console and the right one to [b]button number 4[/b].

To [b]position[/b] one of these cameras, simply grab it with a controller and move it to anywhere in the environment. The [b]zoom level[/b] of the camera can also be adjusted, by moving the controller’s joystick or touchpad up and down (while selecting it with a controller).

[h2]New Environment[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/a1efafb4748d738c27cf10db45a47183b1a518dd.jpg[/img]

This [b]beta [/b]release of Vinyl Reality adds an early version of the new [b]Streaming Studio environment[/b], which is specifically designed for streaming, by making it more visually interesting for people watching a video stream or recording made with Vinyl Reality, from outside of VR on a 2D screen.

Users can customize the environment by playing their own videos on the screens surrounding the DJ booth. More customization features will be added to the environment in upcoming updates.

To find out more about how to load your own videos, check out the [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=how_to_play_custom_videos_on_the_audio_reactive_screens]online documentation on this topic[/url].

[h2]Planned environments for the full release[/h2]
In preparation for the full release of Vinyl Reality, I decided to rethink the environments included with the application, seeing what works and, more importantly, what I think could be improved.

For the final version of the app I'm planning to include 3 different types of environments, each serving a unique purpose:
[list]
[*] [b]Minimal: [/b]Very simple and brightly lit environment, optimized for the best performance. Best suited for practicing and audio recording.
[*] [b]Streaming:[/b] Designed to be as visually interesting as possible for spectators (on a 2D screen), with audio reactive lights, animations and visual effects. Designed to run smoothly on machines meeting the minimum specs. Will allow for some customization.
[*] [b]Experience:[/b] Designed to be as realistic, immersive, visually interesting and awe-inspiring as possible from the perspective of the VR user. Will require a system with recommended specs to run smoothly.
[/list]

The third type (experience) will probably only be added after the application leaves Early Access, because it will take a considerable amount of time and resources to create.

I plan to remove or redesign all of the current environments (Recording Studio, Attic and Club), but still make the current versions available as a separate download, so they can be loaded as a custom environment.

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.0 – Valve Index and Oculus Rift S controller support
notes.content:
Version 1.2.0 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds support for several new controller types, including Valve’s Index controllers and the Oculus Rift S.

[h1]Index Controller Support[/h1]

I have [b]not [/b]yet finished the skeletal input system, which would use finger tracking and touch to interact with objects, so for now the Index controllers still use the same input input system as other controllers.
The control scheme for the Index controllers has been designed to be as intuitive and reliable as possible, but you can always modify it to your personal preferences using the SteamVR controller bindings settings.

I’ve made the “experimental” (and outdated) branch of the application, which contains an [b]unfinished[/b] implementation of the skeletal input system, public for every one who already owns a pair of index controllers to try out. If there is enough interest, I might continue working on the skeletal input version of the application at a later date, so be sure to let me know in the comments below!

[h1]Trackpad input tweaks for mixer knobs[/h1]

I’ve also changed the way rotary knobs on the mixer (ex: EQ knobs) react to trackpad input. To rotate a knob with the trackpad, you now first need to [b]grab the knob[/b] and then slide your thumb [b]up or down[/b] the trackpad. This action mimics rotating the knob between your thumb and index finger and should feel more natural.

I’ve also added two new trackpad related settings to the mixer’s user settings panel: 
[list]
[*] [b]Invert Left Trackpad Input:[/b]
Inverts the direction the knob rotates for the left controller’s trackpad
[*] [b]Trackpad Scroll Range:[/b] 
Controls how many degrees the knob rotates based on the trackpad input
[/list]

A new Mixer Fader Settings panel has been added to the user settings interface. Using this panel, the [b]curves of both the crossfader and channel faders[/b] can be adjusted to adapt to different play styles or situations.

Both fader curves are displayed and updated in real-time to visualize the current settings. The curve describes [b]the volume (y-axis)[/b] in relation to the [b]fader’s position (x-axis)[/b].

[b]Version 1.1.8[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update focuses on improving the functionality of the mixer’s [b]3 band equalizer[/b] as well as fixing some major bugs in the main menu.

Each of the mixer’s 3 band equalizer knobs now has a kill switch function which when activated [b]cuts all the frequencies[/b] for the corresponding range (High, Mid or Low) from the audio signal playing through the channel. The frequency crossover points (Low to Mid and Mid to High) and crossover slope of the mixer’s 3 band equalizer can now be configured using the new mixer settings panel inside the user settings UI. Tweaking these values can be useful to adapt the equalizer to different musical genres.

[b]Version 1.1.3[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. This first update of the new year adds several improvements to the record case.

[h1]Playlists[/h1]

The biggest new feature is the ability to load [b]m3u and m3u8 playlists[/b] in the record case, which makes loading your track collection inside Vinyl Reality a lot easier. This format of playlists can be created in, and exported from, most DJ, media player and music management applications.

Here are a couple of possible use cases for playlists in Vinyl Reality:
[list]
[*] Creating playlists with tracks sorted by BPM, Artist, etc..
[*] Breaking up a large music collection into manageable chunks, without having to move files
[*] Transferring playlists between different apps
[/list]

If playlists files are found in the current directory, they will be displayed in the record case list beneath the directories. To load a playlist, simply select it and use the enter action to open it. If an audio file included in a playlist is missing, it will be marked red in the record case list.

[h1]Performance[/h1]

I’ve also spent a lot of time improving the performance of the record case. In previous versions, loading folders or playlists which contain a large amount of tracks could take a long time, but with this update it should be almost instantaneous.

notes.title: Club Environment – Progress Report
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/c7dee81e3f878b5136a209ea02a62ae72d0307fc.png[/img]

Since I know a lot of you are eagerly awaiting the next update, which will include the brand new club environment, I thought I’d give you all an update on the progress so far.

The last couple of weeks I’ve been mainly focused on programming a system that analyses the audio signal from the mixer in real-time, to detect beats and energy transitions in the music. 
This system will drive all the sound reactive light and visual effects inside the club environment. For example, the colors of the lights will change depending on the energy of the track that’s playing, dimming to warm and soft tones during quiet interludes, to then abruptly change into bright and vivid hues when the beat drops in again.

Here’s a short video showing the new system working its magic in an early version of the club environment: https://youtu.be/JeHTUlQXVmM
For now I’m quite happy with how well the system works. It can adapt to different genres of music and is rather versatile. I will probably keep working on the system after the first iteration of the club environment has been released, to further improve its accuracy and reliability.

Before starting work on the sounds reactive lighting system, I designed the basic layout of the club environment. I tried many different iterations, trying to find a space that feels and looks good from a VR perspective, while keeping in mind performance constraints. The current design I’ve settled on has a strong underground vibe and is heavily inspired by Berlin clubs located in old industrial buildings.

The next couple of weeks I’ll be working on adding details to the club environment as well as adding more lighting and visual effects. If you want to stay up to date with the latest developments, I suggest you join the [url=https://discord.gg/9TCsXfc]Vinyl Reality Discord Server![/url]

notes.content:

The turntable code has been completely rewritten to make it more robust, and to fix the issue where the playback position of records would drift. A small arrow has been added to the record label, which points to the turntable’s needle, when at the start of a track.

A lot of other code has also been rewritten, to make it easier to add new upcoming features. If I have done my job well, none of these code changes should not be noticeable, but in case you should encounter a new bug, be sure to report it.

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.5 – Streaming Console
notes.content:
Version 1.0.5 of Vinyl Reality is now available.

The goal of this update was to make footage recorded with Vinyl Reality more interesting and engaging for your audience to watch, by enabling you to select different camera perspectives to display on the desktop mirror, while recording or streaming your set.

You can switch between the different cameras by selecting the corresponding pad on the bottom row of the new streaming console. The leftmost pad, conveniently labeled [i]HMD[/i],  will display the feed from your headset.

To see what’s possible, be sure to check out this video that was recorded live using the features of the streaming console:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qTJo09_I7Dw

The streaming console also replaces the old audio recorder and adds some extra functionality, including a display which shows the duration and filename of the current recording. 

Please note that the record button on the streaming console [b]only records audio[/b] and [u][b]NOT[/b][/u] video. To record or stream video footage, it’s recommend to use an external tool like OBS Studio, which is free and easy to setup.

The streaming console is currently only available in the brand new [i]Recording Studio[/i] environment, which was designed to be as optimized as possible and should allow you to record your sessions without any performance issues. This environment also includes a screen which displays the feed from the external cameras when they’re activated.

For the next update (1.0.6) I don’t plan to add any new features, but instead I’ll be focusing on improving performance and polishing the content that is already there. This should give me a good foundation to start work on the next major update (1.1.0), which will add a new club environment with interactive light shows and special effects.

[b]Full Release Notes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Added streaming console
[*]Added Recording Studio environment
[*] Removed old audio recorder
[*]Optimized rendering performance
[/list]

If you record your set using the new features added in this update, be sure to share them in the Community Hub!

notes.content:
It took a bit longer than usual, but version 1.0.4 of Vinyl Reality is now available! 

This update focuses on improving the record case's functionality. New features include support for loading several new file formats and displaying track meta data, including BPM.

If a file contains meta data about the track's BPM (Beats Per Minute), this value can now be shown on the turntable's pitch slider. This option can easily be disabled using the settings panel on the application's display mirror.

If a track does not yet contain BPM meta data, it can be added by analyzing it in an external application such as Traktor or MixMeister.

Due to the reading of meta data, opening folders which contain a lot of tracks will now take significantly longer than before, but this will be optimized in the next update. The next update will also add several tools to make streaming your Vinyl Reality sessions more interesting and entertaining.

[*]Added column to record case UI to display directory file count or track BPM value
[*]Added BPM to pitch slider UI

[*]Improved audio signal flow
[/list]
